jobs.title: Analytics Associate Director, US Oncology
jobs.description:
Are you ready to turn complex data into insights that shape oncology strategy and improve commercial performance? As Associate Director, Analytics, U.S. Oncology, you will lead commercial analytics within the U.S. Oncology portfolio, helping teams maximize inline brands and prepare for new launches. You will partner with Marketing and cross-functional colleagues to frame critical business questions and deliver innovative, evidence-based answers in collaboration with Market Research, Data Science, Forecasting, Finance, Market Access, and Data Management.

Key Accountabilities

Partner with stakeholders to define strategic business questions, align priorities, and translate analytical findings into clear, actionable recommendations.
Lead advanced analytics using complex internal and external healthcare data to evaluate brand performance drivers, disease states, patient journeys, and customer behavior.
Serve as a data and analytics expert, ensuring appropriate methods, data interpretation, quality, governance, and compliance while advancing innovative tools and best practices.
Scope, prioritize, and manage multiple analytics projects, balancing business value, timelines, resources, risks, and delivery by internal teams and external agencies.
Build trusted stakeholder relationships, communicate insights effectively to senior leaders, and coach junior analytics colleagues to strengthen collaboration and delivery quality.

This role reports to the Franchise Analytics Director and sits within the Analytics, Data & Reporting function in U.S. Oncology Business Excellence department. The team partners with the U.S. Oncology commercial organization to improve strategic and operational decisions through objective insights, analytics, and performance reporting.

This position is based in Canada.

Essential Skills And Experience

Bachelor’s degree with a preference for a quantitative field.
At least 5 years of experience in analytics, statistics, or a related field, including at least 3 years in the pharmaceutical, biotechnology, or biopharmaceutical consulting sector.
At least 5 years of experience analyzing large, complex healthcare datasets, including claims and electronic health record data.
Demonstrated ability to translate ambiguous business questions into analytical plans and decision-ready recommendations.
Ability to communicate complex analytical concepts clearly to stakeholders.
At least 2 years of experience providing day-to-day direction to internal or external analytics team members.

Preferred Skills And Experience

Advanced degree in a quantitative, scientific, or business discipline.
Commercial analytics experience within oncology.
Experience with predictive modeling, machine learning, or other advanced analytical methods.
Proficiency in SQL, R, Python, or comparable analytical tools.
Experience overseeing business intelligence and data visualization solutions.
Proven project leadership skills, including prioritization, resource coordination, and risk management.

Working at AstraZeneca

When we put unexpected teams in the same room, we spark bold thinking with the power to inspire life-changing medicines. In-person working gives us the platform we need to connect, work at pace, and challenge perceptions.

That’s why we work, on average, a minimum of three days per week from the office. We balance the expectation of being in the office while respecting individual local flexibility.

Why AstraZeneca?

At AstraZeneca's Oncology Business Unit, we are fundamentally changing the way cancer is treated through innovation. We turn our pipeline into reality for more patients, bringing novel and transformative medicines to market. Our pipeline is one of the deepest and broadest in the industry, with innovative science and life-changing medicines to work on today and in the future. We believe in co-creation, harnessing our diverse strengths, and sharing best practices to build the future of our business and industry together. Ready to make your mark on the healthcare ecosystem? Apply now and join us in building the next wave of Oncology!

⠀

Annual base salary for this position ranges from 134,708.00 to 176,804.25.

AstraZeneca is committed to providing fair and equitable compensation opportunities to all colleagues. Our compensation policies and practices have been designed to allow colleagues to progress through the salary range over time as they progress in their role. The range provided in this posting represents an offer pay range used in a majority of situations. The base pay offered will vary depending on multiple individualized factors, including the candidate's skills and experience, job-related knowledge, and other specific business and organizational needs. In some cases, offers outside the range may also be considered to address unique circumstances.

In addition, our permanent positions offer an annual Variable Pay Bonus/Short Term Incentive opportunity as well as eligibility to participate in our equity-based long-term incentive program (if applicable to role). Benefits offered for permanent roles include a competitive Flex Benefits & Retirement Savings Program, 4 weeks’ paid vacation, and annual Personal Days. Fixed Term Contract/Temporary positions (excluding students) are offered a Contract Benefits Program.

jobs.title: Director of Finance And Accounting
jobs.description:
Director of Finance – 3PL / Distribution

Location:
Greater Toronto Area
Work Environment:
On-site
Industry:
Third-Party Logistics (3PL) / Transportation / Distribution

The Opportunity
Our client, an established and growing third-party logistics organization in the Greater Toronto Area, is looking for an experienced Director of Finance
to join its leadership team.
This is a hands-on senior finance position for someone who enjoys being close to the business. In addition to leading the accounting and finance function, the Director of Finance will work closely with operations, transportation, sales, and senior leadership to improve financial performance, strengthen reporting, and provide greater visibility into costs and profitability.
The successful candidate will bring strong financial leadership along with an understanding of the operational side of a logistics, transportation, or distribution business.

Key Responsibilities
Financial Leadership & Reporting
Lead the day-to-day accounting and finance function and provide direction to the finance team.
Oversee financial reporting, general ledger activities, accounts payable, accounts receivable, payroll, and period-end closing.
Deliver timely and accurate monthly, quarterly, and annual financial reporting.
Lead the budgeting and forecasting process and maintain ongoing cash flow projections.
Analyze business performance, operating expenses, customer profitability, and gross margins.
Provide senior leadership with meaningful financial analysis to support business decisions.
Maintain appropriate financial controls, policies, and processes.
Manage relationships with external auditors, financial institutions, tax professionals, and other external partners.

Commercial Finance & Profitability
Work closely with operational and commercial teams to understand the financial performance of customers, lanes, services, and contracts.
Provide financial oversight related to transportation costs, pricing, and margin performance.
Review costing information and identify areas where profitability can be improved.
Support pricing decisions, customer proposals, bids, and contract renewals.
Develop reporting that provides greater visibility into customer and operational profitability.
Help establish consistent processes for reviewing pricing, costs, and margins.

Business & Operational Partnership
Partner with Operations and Transportation leaders to ensure financial information accurately reflects business activity.
Provide financial guidance on operational decisions, service costs, and customer requirements.
Work with Sales on the financial components of new business opportunities and customer agreements.
Develop and monitor KPIs related to financial and operational performance.
Identify trends, risks, and opportunities and translate financial data into practical recommendations for the leadership team.

Payroll, Compliance & Risk
Provide oversight of payroll administration and related reporting requirements.
Ensure appropriate remittances, tax filings, and regulatory requirements are completed accurately and on time.
Maintain strong financial documentation and ensure the organization remains audit-ready.
Monitor areas of financial and operational risk and ensure appropriate controls are in place.

Leadership & Continuous Improvement
Coach, develop, and support members of the finance team.
Evaluate existing financial processes and identify opportunities to improve efficiency, accuracy, and reporting.
Support improvements to accounting, transportation, and business systems.
Participate in system implementations and integrations, with a focus on data integrity and effective financial reporting.
Introduce tools, reporting, and automation that provide leadership with better and faster business information.

Qualifications
Bachelor’s degree in Accounting, Finance, Business, or a related discipline.
CPA designation strongly preferred.

Progressive experience in accounting and financial leadership within 3PL, transportation, logistics, distribution, or a similar operational environment
.
Strong understanding of financial reporting, budgeting, forecasting, cash flow, and internal controls.
Experience analyzing costing, margins, pricing, and profitability
within an operational business.
Previous experience leading and developing a finance or accounting team.
Strong Excel skills and experience working with accounting and ERP systems.
Exposure to transportation management systems (TMS) or other logistics technology is considered an asset.
Experience supporting system implementations, integrations, or finance process improvements is an asset.
Strong analytical, leadership, and communication skills with the ability to work effectively across multiple departments.

The Ideal Candidate
You are a finance leader who wants to understand why the numbers look the way they do
, not simply report them.

You are comfortable moving between financial statements and operational conversations and can work collaboratively with Operations, Sales, and senior leadership. You understand the importance of costing and margin visibility in a high-volume logistics environment and can turn financial information into practical business decisions.

This opportunity is well suited to someone who has built their career within a 3PL, transportation, logistics, distribution, or similarly fast-paced operational business
and is looking for a role where Finance has a meaningful seat at the table.

Employment Equity & Accessibility
Our client is committed to providing an inclusive and accessible recruitment process. We welcome applications from all qualified individuals and are committed to employment practices that are free from discrimination and harassment.
Accommodations are available upon request for candidates taking part in all aspects of the recruitment and selection process, in accordance with the Accessibility for Ontarians with Disabilities Act (AODA)
and the Ontario Human Rights Code
.
In accordance with Ontario employment legislation, applicants are advised that artificial intelligence (AI) may be used during the recruitment and selection process to assist with screening or assessing applications
.
We thank all applicants for their interest; however, only those selected for an interview will be contacted.

jobs.title: Vice President, Finance
jobs.description:
Who we are

Kilmer Group is a multi-generational platform for business development and investment, built on operational excellence, long-term stewardship, and trusted relationships. Headquartered in Toronto, we invest across three core sectors: Private Equity, Infrastructure & Real Estate, and Sports & Media, partnering with exceptional management teams to build and grow enduring businesses.

Kilmer Group has built a reputation for disciplined investment, active ownership, and creating long-term value. Our approach is grounded in partnership, integrity, and a commitment to building businesses that generate lasting impact for our partners, stakeholders, and the communities we serve.

Who we need

Reporting to the CFO, we are hiring a Vice President, Finance to play a key leadership role across Kilmer Group's finance function. As our new Vice President, Finance, you will combine financial stewardship with strategic partnership, helping guide decisions that support the continued growth and evolution of a diversified investment platform. Working closely with the CFO, senior leaders, and investment teams, you will oversee financial reporting, treasury, budgeting, investment portfolio reporting, and governance while providing the financial insight that supports investment decisions, business performance, and long-term value creation. You will lead a finance team and contribute across a broad range of initiatives, from evaluating acquisitions and investments to strengthening reporting, improving processes, and building the financial capabilities and infrastructure needed to support the organization's continued growth.

This is an existing, full-time opportunity based in the Toronto office, working onsite five days per week.

What’s in it for you?

Strategic influence. Reporting directly to the CFO, you will act as a trusted partner to the executive leadership team, contributing financial insight that informs investment decisions, capital allocation, and the long-term direction of Kilmer Group.

Breadth and exposure. This is an opportunity to apply your expertise across a diverse investment portfolio rather than within a single operating business. You will work on initiatives spanning financial reporting, tax, budgeting, long-term forecasting, governance, and business performance.

Build what's next. Technology and AI are transforming the finance function, and Kilmer Group is evolving with it - strengthening reporting, deepening financial analysis, and modernizing our processes to harness these new tools. You will help build new capabilities, grow a high-performing team, and shape a financial foundation built for long-term success.

As our new VP Finance, you will

Lead the finance function.
You will oversee accounting, treasury, financial reporting, and cash management across a complex, multi-entity organization, ensuring strong controls, effective budgeting, and timely, accurate reporting. As a trusted partner to the CFO, you will provide the financial leadership and operational oversight that enables the team to deliver with confidence while supporting the organization's growth objectives.
Provide strategic financial insight.
You will translate financial information into meaningful analysis that supports executive decision-making. Working closely with the CFO and senior leaders, you will develop reporting and insights that strengthen planning, support investment decisions, and provide a clearer understanding of business performance across the organization.
Support investments and corporate growth.
You will partner with the investment team on acquisitions, portfolio reporting, valuations, due diligence, and other strategic initiatives. You will work closely with leaders across Kilmer Group and its portfolio companies, providing financial guidance and building trusted relationships that support long-term value creation.
Lead and develop the team.
You will mentor, coach, and support the continued growth of the finance team while fostering a collaborative, accountable, and low-ego environment. You will build capability and create opportunities for continuous learning amongst the team.

You bring

The leadership.
You have experience leading high-performing finance teams and fostering a culture of accountability, collaboration, and continuous improvement. You are a trusted advisor who can balance strategic priorities with operational execution while building strong relationships across the organization.
The foundation.
You are a CPA, CA with experience gained in both public accounting and industry, ideally including a Big 4 audit environment. You bring strong technical knowledge of ASPE and IFRS, investment holding company accounting, including asset valuations and investee reporting. You have experience with compliance and risk to ensure adherence with tax laws, accounting standards and internal controls. You know how to apply this technical foundation in a commercial environment, combining accounting expertise with sound strategic and business judgment.
The financial expertise.
You bring experience across financial reporting, treasury, budgeting, cash management, tax and corporate governance within complex organizations. You have worked with investment portfolios, valuations, transactions, or corporate development activities and are comfortable partnering with senior leaders to support investment decisions and long-term value creation.
The analytical mindset.
You are naturally curious and continuously look for ways to improve how work gets done. You leverage data and technology to strengthen reporting and decision-making, and you are excited by the opportunity to modernize finance through automation and the thoughtful application of AI.
The communication skills.
You can translate complex financial information into clear recommendations that support decision-making. Whether working with executives, portfolio company leaders, auditors, or external advisors, you build credibility through sound judgment, strong communication, and a collaborative approach.

Why join Kilmer Group?

Today, Kilmer Group continues to build on decades of successful investment and business leadership offering a dynamic and supportive environment with opportunities for growth and development. Beyond our investments, we are committed to strengthening the communities where we live and work through initiatives that support sport, health, research, and community development. Joining Kilmer Group means becoming part of an organization that thinks for the long term, values partnership, and is committed to building a lasting legacy.

Join us

We recognize that no candidate brings every qualification to a role. If your experience is closely aligned with what we are looking for and you are excited by the opportunity to contribute to Kilmer Group, we encourage you to apply. We look forward to learning more about your experience and the perspective you would bring to our team.

What you can expect from our interview process

A virtual interview with a Talent Advisor to discuss your interest in joining Kilmer Group and your experience. The conversation will be recorded using BrightHire, an AI-powered video interview tool. More details will be shared when you are invited to interview.
An in-person conversation with the Chief Financial Officer to discuss your leadership experience, your approach to building high-performing finance functions, and how you partner with executives to support investment decisions and long-term growth.
An in-person presentation and discussion with the Vice President, Talent and Special Projects and a senior member of the finance team. You will be asked to prepare and present a case study, followed by a conversation about your thinking, priorities, and leadership approach.
A final in-person conversation with the Chief Financial Officer to explore mutual fit, discuss your vision for the role, and answer any remaining questions. Finalists may also have the opportunity to meet additional members of the leadership team.

Kilmer Group is committed to creating a workplace where people are treated with respect, supported in their development, and empowered to contribute their best work. We recognize that diverse perspectives strengthen our business and help us make better decisions for our organization, our partners, and the communities in which we operate.

We welcome applications from all qualified candidates and are committed to providing an accessible recruitment process. If you require accommodation at any stage of the recruitment process, please let us know and we will work with you to meet your needs.

jobs.title: Head of Financial Reporting
jobs.description:
Some reporting roles ask you to maintain what already exists. This one asks you to transform it.

Reporting to the VP Finance, this opportunity is for a financial reporting leader who wants more than a steady-state mandate. The role offers meaningful autonomy to bring structure, discipline and momentum to a Finance function in transformation, while strengthening public company reporting and elevating technical accounting capability.

The successful candidate will bring experience from strong reporting environments and the confidence to apply that perspective in a setting where processes, standards and team capability can still be shaped. For a leader energized by complexity, this is an opportunity to build something better and create lasting impact.

The Opportunity

A mandate for a financial reporting leader who wants to combine public company rigor, technical accounting depth, process improvement and people leadership. This is an opportunity to shape how the function operates, develop the team and create the structure needed for a more confident, scalable and effective Finance organization.

What You'll Own

Lead quarterly and annual public company reporting: external financial statements, disclosures, and review processes under IFRS.
Act as technical accounting advisor for the Finance organization — interpreting, documenting, and applying IFRS guidance with practical judgment, including potential US GAAP considerations.
Prepare and review technical accounting memos on complex, judgmental matters (goodwill, impairment, significant estimates) for auditors and senior stakeholders.
Support accounting for M&A, integration, and divestiture activity as it arises.
Partner directly with external auditors, ensuring issues are well-prepared, well-documented, and resolved credibly.
Drive continuous improvement in reporting processes, controls, documentation, and review standards.
Lead, coach, and grow a team — including a planned Senior Manager, Technical Accounting hire.
Build trusted relationships across Finance, Tax, and senior/C-suite stakeholders.

What You Bring

CPA/CA designation, ideally grounded in public accounting.
Progressive public company financial reporting experience — you've owned a reporting process end to end.
Strong IFRS technical accounting and public company reporting experience, including confidence supporting a potential US GAAP conversion
Demonstrated technical accounting depth: writing/reviewing memos on complex, non-routine matters.
M&A-related accounting exposure is a strong asset.
A track record of process improvement in environments still being built or refined.
Proven people leadership — coaching, performance management, development.
Comfort with ambiguity, fast pace, and change.

How You Lead

You own the details without losing the bigger picture.
You bring strong reporting discipline and technical judgment, while staying pragmatic and business-minded.
You hold an uncompromising standard for quality — and get there without friction.
You're proactive and resourceful, comfortable engaging unfamiliar stakeholders to move work forward.
You communicate clearly and build trust without an aggressive style.
You develop people deliberately and address performance directly, constructively, and fairly.
You bring credibility and maturity to conversations with senior leaders, auditors, and the C-suite.

If you are a public company financial reporting leader who wants more than a steady-state mandate, this is an opportunity to build, improve and shape a function with meaningful autonomy, visibility and impact.

Don't wait and apply in confidence.

jobs.title: Assistant Vice-President, Research Strategy and Services
jobs.description:
McGill University is seeking an accomplished and collaborative leader to assume the role of Assistant Vice-President, Research Strategy and Services (AVP).
Reporting to the Vice-President, Research and Innovation, the AVP is responsible for advancing McGill University's research enterprise through strategic leadership of research development, sponsored research services, and institutional research planning. As a member of the senior leadership team within the Research and Innovation portfolio, the AVP oversees a complex portfolio that supports researchers, research teams, Faculties, affiliated hospitals, and research institutes across the research funding lifecycle, while helping to strengthen the University's capacity for research excellence and impact.

The AVP leads the University's efforts to develop and advance major institutional research initiatives, including high-profile national and international funding competitions. Working closely with the Vice-President, Research and Innovation, academic leaders, affiliated hospitals, and external partners, the AVP strengthens McGill's research enterprise by fostering interdisciplinary collaboration, supporting institution-wide research priorities, and enhancing the University's capacity to secure and manage major research investments. As a senior advisor and institutional representative, the AVP provides leadership on research strategy, policy, governance, infrastructure planning, and performance measurement, while representing the University with governments, funding agencies, foundations, industry partners, and peer institutions to advance McGill's research mission and global reputation.

This is an exciting time to join McGill University and contribute to advancing the University’s ambitious research agenda, including the implementation of McGill’s 2026 – 2031 Strategic Research Plan. Following a comprehensive review of research support services, the Research and Innovation portfolio is implementing a new integrated Research Ecosystem model that brings together pre-award and post-award functions to create a more coordinated, efficient, and researcher-centered service environment. The AVP will lead this transformation, cultivating a culture of service excellence, collaboration, accountability, and continuous improvement while ensuring researchers receive timely, strategic, and solutions-oriented support.

The ideal candidate will possess a graduate degree and a demonstrated record of progressive senior leadership in research administration, research strategy, or research development within a large, complex organization, preferably in a university, research-intensive, or public-sector environment. They will bring deep knowledge of the Canadian research funding landscape, experience leading institutional research initiatives and partnerships, and a proven ability to navigate complexity while driving organizational effectiveness and service excellence. Success in this role will require strategic leadership, exceptional relationship-building skills, sound judgment, and the ability to lead high-performing teams while aligning people, processes, and resources in support of the University’s ambitious research priorities. Bilingualism in English and French is required.

McGill University has partnered with the leadership advisory firm Odgers for this recruitment. Applications are encouraged immediately to Michael Williams, Andrea Patrick and Krutika Hotwani at https://careers.odgers.com/en-ca/job/32099. This is an existing vacancy. The new AVP will assume the position in early 2027.

Inquiries or accommodation requests can be directed to mcgillavp@odgers.com.

Pour voir l'annonce en français, rendez-vous sur : https://careers.odgers.com/fr-ca/job/32099

Founded in 1821, McGill University has established a strong reputation for being a leader in higher education globally, distinguished by the excellence of its faculty, the dedication of its staff, the talent and quality of its students, the contributions of its 325,000 alumni, and its exceptional record in both teaching and research. McGill is the top medical-doctoral university and the most internationally diverse research-intensive public university in Canada, with approximately 30% of students from more than 150 countries. The University is home to over 40,000 students and over 13,000 employees spanning 11 faculties, 13 professional schools and over 300 programs of study. McGill’s exceptional faculty and alumni- which include 12 Nobel Prize winners and 149 Rhodes scholars - are recognized for their scientific and technological breakthroughs and for examining the social, environmental, ethical and policy impacts of business practices, technology, science, and medicine; 184 are Canada Research Chairs and 209 are active Fellows of the Royal Society of Canada. McGill offers faculty, staff, and students a cohesive university-wide environment of academic excellence that is second to none, where the community is stimulated to push the boundaries of knowledge creation in every field imaginable. For more information about McGill, please visit www.mcgill.ca.

McGill University is committed to equity and diversity within its community and values academic rigour and excellence. We welcome and encourage applications from all qualified candidates including racialized persons/visible minorities, women, Indigenous persons, persons with disabilities, ethnic minorities, and persons of minority sexual orientations and gender identities with the skills and knowledge to engage productively with diverse communities.

At McGill, research that reflects diverse intellectual traditions, methodologies, and modes of dissemination and translation is valued and encouraged. Candidates are invited to demonstrate their research impact both within and across academic disciplines and in other sectors, such as government, communities, or industry.

All qualified applicants are encouraged to apply; however, in accordance with Canadian immigration requirements, Canadians and permanent residents will be given priority.

jobs.title: Director, Global Business Planning (FP&A)
jobs.description:
Your Opportunity at ARC’TERYX:

As the Director, Global Business Planning, you will serve as the connective tissue of Arc'teryx's global financial planning process. You will own the consolidation of all regional financial plans, including annual budgets and quarterly forecasts, into a coherent, enterprise-wide view, enabling leadership to make informed decisions with speed and confidence. This is a high-visibility, high-impact role that operates at the intersection of financial planning, strategic insight, and executive communication.

You will serve as the primary architect of our financial planning calendar and cadence, partnering closely with regional and global FP&A teams to drive alignment, consistency, and analytical rigor across the enterprise. You will also own the financial systems infrastructure, reporting frameworks, and capital planning processes that power Arc'teryx's ability to plan and perform at a global scale.

This role is based out of our North Vancouver office. Candidates must be eligible to work in Canada.

Meet Your Future Team:

The Global FP&A team at Arc'teryx sits at the center of enterprise financial decision-making. We are responsible for translating regional and functional performance into a unified financial narrative, providing leadership with the clarity to review past results, understand business drivers, and plan confidently for the future. We work closely with regional finance partners across North America, China, EMEA, and APAC, as well as functional leaders across the business, to deliver insights that matter.

If you were in the Director, Global Business Planning role now, here are some of the core activities you would be doing:

Owning the end-to-end consolidation of all regional financial plans, including annual budgets and quarterly forecasts, into an integrated global view across P&L, and capital expenditures

Leading enterprise-wide variance analysis, comparing actuals to budget and forecast, and synthesizing insights into clear, executive-ready commentary that explains the 'so what' behind the numbers

Serving as the primary finance lead for Quarterly Business Reviews (QBR), Board of Directors (BOD) materials, and investor-facing financial narratives, partnering closely with the CFO and VP of FP&A on preparation and delivery

Building and maintaining the global financial planning calendar, coordinating planning cycles across regional FP&A teams to ensure timely, consistent, and high-quality submissions

Owning and continuously improving Arc'teryx's financial systems infrastructure, including OneStream, PowerBI, and Oracle, to ensure accurate, efficient, and scalable financial reporting and planning capabilities

Developing and managing enterprise-level financial analytics and insights capabilities, including standardized KPI frameworks, executive dashboards, and performance reporting tools

Leading capital planning processes, including tracking of capital expenditure budgets, return-on-investment analysis, and reporting to senior leadership and the Board

Acting as a key connector between regional FP&A teams and global finance leadership, fostering collaboration, knowledge-sharing, and best practice alignment across geographies

Driving continuous improvement in planning processes, reporting accuracy, and analytical capabilities through automation, systems enhancements, and process redesign

Supporting ad-hoc strategic analysis requests from executive leadership, including scenario modelling, business case development, and financial due diligence

Here are some of the things you could be working on in the future:

Building Arc'teryx's next-generation financial planning and reporting infrastructure to support the company's growth and increased organizational complexity

Expanding the Global FP&A team's analytics capabilities through AI-driven forecasting, predictive modelling, and automated insight generation

Acting as a thought partner to the CFO and C-suite on capital allocation priorities, financial strategy, and enterprise planning governance

Representing Global FP&A in cross-functional initiatives related to ERP transformation, data strategy, and digital finance evolution

Are you our next Director, Global Business Planning?

You have 10+ years of progressive experience in FP&A, corporate finance, or strategic finance, with at least 3 years in a senior leadership role with global or multi-regional scope

You have a bachelor's degree in finance, accounting, economics, or equivalent, and ideally hold a CPA, CFA, or MBA

You have deep expertise in financial consolidation and enterprise planning processes, budget cycles, quarterly forecasts, and long-range plans, across multiple business units or geographies

You have a strong command of financial systems and planning tools (OneStream, Oracle, SAP, or equivalent), with demonstrated ability to drive systems improvements and reporting automation

You are an exceptional communicator who can translate complex financial data into clear, compelling narratives for executive and Board-level audiences

You have experience preparing and supporting QBR and Board of Directors materials, with an understanding of what leadership needs to make high-stakes decisions

You have advanced analytical and modelling skills, with proficiency in Excel, PowerBI, and other data visualization tools

You are a collaborative, trust-building leader who can influence without authority and drive alignment across regional and functional teams

You thrive in fast-moving, ambiguous environments and can manage multiple high-priority workstreams simultaneously without sacrificing quality

You are proactive in identifying the root cause of issues and developing scalable, cross-functional solutions

You inspire breakthrough thinking and continuous improvement in the teams and processes you touch

Your passion for your work is paralleled by your passion for getting outside and living it

Compensation:
The salary range for this role is CAD$149,000 - CAD$195,000 

Total Rewards

Most new team members join between the start and midpoint of the range, where you can contribute right away while continuing to grow your craft, your collaborations, and your impact at Arc’teryx. This range reflects market alignment and the scope of the role. Individual pay is determined by your skills, experience, and level of responsibility.

We’re committed to fair, equitable, and competitive pay, reviewed regularly to ensure internal alignment and market relevance. Transparency is part of how we follow through on our commitments and how we honour the value you bring to our team.

In addition to base pay, Arc’teryx supports people through benefits designed to sustain both work and life:

y - Paid time off, wellness time, and No Wasted Day program (dedicated paid days to get outside & explore).

  *Eligibility for certain programs may vary by role.

Equal Opportunity

WESTERN CANADA (NORTH)

About The Role

Our client, a First Nation located in the North within Western Canada is currently seeking a Director of Finance to join their team. Reporting directly to the CAO and working on behalf of the Nation and its community members, the Director of Finance is responsible for the day-to-day accounting and financial management, oversight of the financial administration and ensuring compliance with accounting standards. The Director of Finance plays a critical role in supporting continued growth, providing financial insight and strategic advice in partnership with the CAO, and is hands on in their direct responsibilities of financial reporting, budgeting and internal controls.

Key Responsibilities

Budgeting & Financial Planning

Lead the development and integration of the annual budget
Consolidate department budgets, evaluate accuracy and alignment with strategic goals.
Create multi-year financial plan, capital plans, and risk management plans for presentation and CAO review

Financial Reporting

Prepare and present monthly, quarterly, and annual financial statements, and ad hoc financial reports

Our client, an established and growing third-party logistics organization in the Greater Toronto Area, is looking for an experienced Director of Finance
to join its leadership team.
This is a hands-on senior finance position for someone who enjoys being close to the business. In addition to leading the accounting and finance function, the Director of Finance will work closely with operations, transportation, sales, and senior leadership to improve financial performance, strengthen reporting, and provide greater visibility into costs and profitability.
The successful candidate will bring strong financial leadership along with an understanding of the operational side of a logistics, transportation, or distribution business.

Key Responsibilities
Financial Leadership & Reporting
Lead the day-to-day accounting and finance function and provide direction to the finance team.
Oversee financial reporting, general ledger activities, accounts payable, accounts receivable, payroll, and period-end closing.

Analyze business performance, operating expenses, customer profitability, and gross margins.
Provide senior leadership with meaningful financial analysis to support business decisions.
Maintain appropriate financial controls, policies, and processes.

Commercial Finance & Profitability
Work closely with operational and commercial teams to understand the financial performance of customers, lanes, services, and contracts.
Provide financial oversight related to transportation costs, pricing, and margin performance.
Review costing information and identify areas where profitability can be improved.
Support pricing decisions, customer proposals, bids, and contract renewals.
Develop reporting that provides greater visibility into customer and operational profitability.

Business & Operational Partnership
Partner with Operations and Transportation leaders to ensure financial information accurately reflects business activity.
Provide financial guidance on operational decisions, service costs, and customer requirements.

Identify trends, risks, and opportunities and translate financial data into practical recommendations for the leadership team.

new_jobs.title: Vice President, Finance
new_jobs.description:
Who we are

Kilmer Group is a multi-generational platform for business development and investment, built on operational excellence, long-term stewardship, and trusted relationships. Headquartered in Toronto, we invest across three core sectors: Private Equity, Infrastructure & Real Estate, and Sports & Media, partnering with exceptional management teams to build and grow enduring businesses.

Kilmer Group has built a reputation for disciplined investment, active ownership, and creating long-term value. Our approach is grounded in partnership, integrity, and a commitment to building businesses that generate lasting impact for our partners, stakeholders, and the communities we serve.

Who we need

Reporting to the CFO, we are hiring a Vice President, Finance to play a key leadership role across Kilmer Group's finance function. As our new Vice President, Finance, you will combine financial stewardship with strategic partnership, helping guide decisions that support the continued growth and evolution of a diversified investment platform. Working closely with the CFO, senior leaders, and investment teams, you will oversee financial reporting, treasury, budgeting, investment portfolio reporting, and governance while providing the financial insight that supports investment decisions, business performance, and long-term value creation. You will lead a finance team and contribute across a broad range of initiatives, from evaluating acquisitions and investments to strengthening reporting, improving processes, and building the financial capabilities and infrastructure needed to support the organization's continued growth.

This is an existing, full-time opportunity based in the Toronto office, working onsite five days per week.

What’s in it for you?

Strategic influence. Reporting directly to the CFO, you will act as a trusted partner to the executive leadership team, contributing financial insight that informs investment decisions, capital allocation, and the long-term direction of Kilmer Group.

Breadth and exposure. This is an opportunity to apply your expertise across a diverse investment portfolio rather than within a single operating business. You will work on initiatives spanning financial reporting, tax, budgeting, long-term forecasting, governance, and business performance.

Build what's next. Technology and AI are transforming the finance function, and Kilmer Group is evolving with it - strengthening reporting, deepening financial analysis, and modernizing our processes to harness these new tools. You will help build new capabilities, grow a high-performing team, and shape a financial foundation built for long-term success.

As our new VP Finance, you will

Lead the finance function.
You will oversee accounting, treasury, financial reporting, and cash management across a complex, multi-entity organization, ensuring strong controls, effective budgeting, and timely, accurate reporting. As a trusted partner to the CFO, you will provide the financial leadership and operational oversight that enables the team to deliver with confidence while supporting the organization's growth objectives.
Provide strategic financial insight.
You will translate financial information into meaningful analysis that supports executive decision-making. Working closely with the CFO and senior leaders, you will develop reporting and insights that strengthen planning, support investment decisions, and provide a clearer understanding of business performance across the organization.
Support investments and corporate growth.
You will partner with the investment team on acquisitions, portfolio reporting, valuations, due diligence, and other strategic initiatives. You will work closely with leaders across Kilmer Group and its portfolio companies, providing financial guidance and building trusted relationships that support long-term value creation.
Lead and develop the team.
You will mentor, coach, and support the continued growth of the finance team while fostering a collaborative, accountable, and low-ego environment. You will build capability and create opportunities for continuous learning amongst the team.

You bring

The leadership.
You have experience leading high-performing finance teams and fostering a culture of accountability, collaboration, and continuous improvement. You are a trusted advisor who can balance strategic priorities with operational execution while building strong relationships across the organization.
The foundation.
You are a CPA, CA with experience gained in both public accounting and industry, ideally including a Big 4 audit environment. You bring strong technical knowledge of ASPE and IFRS, investment holding company accounting, including asset valuations and investee reporting. You have experience with compliance and risk to ensure adherence with tax laws, accounting standards and internal controls. You know how to apply this technical foundation in a commercial environment, combining accounting expertise with sound strategic and business judgment.
The financial expertise.
You bring experience across financial reporting, treasury, budgeting, cash management, tax and corporate governance within complex organizations. You have worked with investment portfolios, valuations, transactions, or corporate development activities and are comfortable partnering with senior leaders to support investment decisions and long-term value creation.
The analytical mindset.
You are naturally curious and continuously look for ways to improve how work gets done. You leverage data and technology to strengthen reporting and decision-making, and you are excited by the opportunity to modernize finance through automation and the thoughtful application of AI.
The communication skills.
You can translate complex financial information into clear recommendations that support decision-making. Whether working with executives, portfolio company leaders, auditors, or external advisors, you build credibility through sound judgment, strong communication, and a collaborative approach.

Why join Kilmer Group?

Today, Kilmer Group continues to build on decades of successful investment and business leadership offering a dynamic and supportive environment with opportunities for growth and development. Beyond our investments, we are committed to strengthening the communities where we live and work through initiatives that support sport, health, research, and community development. Joining Kilmer Group means becoming part of an organization that thinks for the long term, values partnership, and is committed to building a lasting legacy.

Join us

We recognize that no candidate brings every qualification to a role. If your experience is closely aligned with what we are looking for and you are excited by the opportunity to contribute to Kilmer Group, we encourage you to apply. We look forward to learning more about your experience and the perspective you would bring to our team.

What you can expect from our interview process

A virtual interview with a Talent Advisor to discuss your interest in joining Kilmer Group and your experience. The conversation will be recorded using BrightHire, an AI-powered video interview tool. More details will be shared when you are invited to interview.
An in-person conversation with the Chief Financial Officer to discuss your leadership experience, your approach to building high-performing finance functions, and how you partner with executives to support investment decisions and long-term growth.
An in-person presentation and discussion with the Vice President, Talent and Special Projects and a senior member of the finance team. You will be asked to prepare and present a case study, followed by a conversation about your thinking, priorities, and leadership approach.
A final in-person conversation with the Chief Financial Officer to explore mutual fit, discuss your vision for the role, and answer any remaining questions. Finalists may also have the opportunity to meet additional members of the leadership team.

Kilmer Group is committed to creating a workplace where people are treated with respect, supported in their development, and empowered to contribute their best work. We recognize that diverse perspectives strengthen our business and help us make better decisions for our organization, our partners, and the communities in which we operate.

We welcome applications from all qualified candidates and are committed to providing an accessible recruitment process. If you require accommodation at any stage of the recruitment process, please let us know and we will work with you to meet your needs.

new_jobs.title: Assistant Vice-President, Research Strategy and Services
new_jobs.description:
McGill University is seeking an accomplished and collaborative leader to assume the role of Assistant Vice-President, Research Strategy and Services (AVP).
Reporting to the Vice-President, Research and Innovation, the AVP is responsible for advancing McGill University's research enterprise through strategic leadership of research development, sponsored research services, and institutional research planning. As a member of the senior leadership team within the Research and Innovation portfolio, the AVP oversees a complex portfolio that supports researchers, research teams, Faculties, affiliated hospitals, and research institutes across the research funding lifecycle, while helping to strengthen the University's capacity for research excellence and impact.

The AVP leads the University's efforts to develop and advance major institutional research initiatives, including high-profile national and international funding competitions. Working closely with the Vice-President, Research and Innovation, academic leaders, affiliated hospitals, and external partners, the AVP strengthens McGill's research enterprise by fostering interdisciplinary collaboration, supporting institution-wide research priorities, and enhancing the University's capacity to secure and manage major research investments. As a senior advisor and institutional representative, the AVP provides leadership on research strategy, policy, governance, infrastructure planning, and performance measurement, while representing the University with governments, funding agencies, foundations, industry partners, and peer institutions to advance McGill's research mission and global reputation.

This is an exciting time to join McGill University and contribute to advancing the University’s ambitious research agenda, including the implementation of McGill’s 2026 – 2031 Strategic Research Plan. Following a comprehensive review of research support services, the Research and Innovation portfolio is implementing a new integrated Research Ecosystem model that brings together pre-award and post-award functions to create a more coordinated, efficient, and researcher-centered service environment. The AVP will lead this transformation, cultivating a culture of service excellence, collaboration, accountability, and continuous improvement while ensuring researchers receive timely, strategic, and solutions-oriented support.

The ideal candidate will possess a graduate degree and a demonstrated record of progressive senior leadership in research administration, research strategy, or research development within a large, complex organization, preferably in a university, research-intensive, or public-sector environment. They will bring deep knowledge of the Canadian research funding landscape, experience leading institutional research initiatives and partnerships, and a proven ability to navigate complexity while driving organizational effectiveness and service excellence. Success in this role will require strategic leadership, exceptional relationship-building skills, sound judgment, and the ability to lead high-performing teams while aligning people, processes, and resources in support of the University’s ambitious research priorities. Bilingualism in English and French is required.

McGill University has partnered with the leadership advisory firm Odgers for this recruitment. Applications are encouraged immediately to Michael Williams, Andrea Patrick and Krutika Hotwani at https://careers.odgers.com/en-ca/job/32099. This is an existing vacancy. The new AVP will assume the position in early 2027.

Inquiries or accommodation requests can be directed to mcgillavp@odgers.com.
